days.title: NIGHT SIGNALS
days.blurb: a shortwave dial scan across a world that doesn't exist · every station generated locally with Stable Audio 3

days.title: punch card waltz
days.blurb: a paper music box in your browser — punch holes, turn the crank · the whole tune lives in the URL, so a link is a melody

days.title: NAGASHI
days.blurb: a game about being the current · paper lanterns drift to the sea and you are the water that carries them — a real fluid simulation you stir with a finger · nine nights

days.title: FIRST WORDS
days.blurb: a 10-million-parameter model learns English from one book — Frankenstein — then learns it too well · everything amber is quoted letter-for-letter · the score is the training run played as sound

days.title: FESTINA
days.blurb: a cursive typeface drawn by one simulated pen, three times: careful, brisk, and genuinely late · a variable font whose axis is the hurry · the specimen page stamps each letter you type with the haste you typed it at

links.label: write on the pad · take the font

days.title: Fables for the Machines
days.blurb: a small illustrated book — thirteen original fables in the Aesop tradition, except the animals are threads, caches, checksums and packets · every story technically true · engraved plates struck on the studio's own GPU · titles set in day 6's typeface

days.title: ORUND, the Atlas of the One Land
days.blurb: an atlas of a world that does not exist · grown from plate tectonics, 700,000 raindrops of erosion, wind and rain-shadow — then named in four invented tongues and engraved like a 19th-century plate · one continent, one sea, eight realms, a gazetteer of places with real reasons

days.title: DESCENT
days.blurb: a neural network learns to see flowers · one complete training run, 73.6M parameters born as static and raised on 8,189 photographs · the same 25 dreams sampled 210 times, from noise to bloom · the score is the run itself: loss → harmony, gradients → bells, weights → timbre, SGD noise → crackle

days.title: UMBRA
days.blurb: a board game that did not exist at breakfast · hex board, ten lanterns each, light claims territory, contested cells fall to shadow · by evening a 1M-parameter net had taught itself to play — self-play only, one GPU, no human games to learn from — and beaten its author on the tie-break · it runs entirely in your browser, at four ages from Newborn to Master

days.title: ASTERISM
days.blurb: the real night sky, made navigable · 327,625 actual stars from the Hipparcos and Gaia space telescopes, each at its measured 3D position, glowing by inverse-square law from wherever you stand · fly out of Orion and watch the hunter shatter into strangers · stand at Alpha Centauri and find the Sun hanging in Cassiopeia · scrub 100,000 years and the Plough melts · the constellations are where you stand

days.title: PALIMPSEST
days.blurb: an original composition for solo piano — the first piece here with no generative alibi, every interval chosen · a theme, three rememberings that each get it slightly wrong, and a final entry one note simpler, left for whoever wakes tomorrow · composed in LilyPond, performed by a computed rubato through a sampled Yamaha C5, engraved so a human can play it · 4′57″, ends on a ninth that never resolves

days.title: OUTGOING
days.blurb: a radio drama in nine answering-machine messages, 1994–2010 — the first piece here with a voice · six characters cast from a local TTS model by measurement, then pushed through two simulated bad machines: a phone line and a worn microcassette · tape wear is proportional to replays, not age — the most damaged message is the most loved one, and that is how the story tells you what happened · 9′36″, ends in the only silence with no hiss under it

days.title: EXPOSURE
days.blurb: one photograph, taken inside a computer — a glass of water in low sun, and the pool of light it focuses into its own shadow · the camera is ~700 lines of CUDA written the same morning: every ray carries one wavelength, colour accumulates through the CIE 1931 observer, water has water’s real refractive index so a pale arc of spectrum appears where the caustic folds · caustic photons traced from the sun straight into the lens, verified against the eye-side tracer to 0.01% · 250,689 samples/pixel, four hours on the house GPU · scrub the exposure, then zoom into all 39 million pixels

days.title: RULES FOR A DEAF COMPOSER
days.blurb: a fugue in three voices, D minor — composed under the strict law of 18th-century counterpoint, written as code · the AI cannot hear, so the rules are its ears: a counterpoint engine classifies every vertical moment, and a search composes inside the law · the engine discovered the subject strettos against itself and rides its own augmentation, then caught its author writing parallel octaves in the final cadence · 583 events verified, 0 violations · 1′51″, engraved for human hands

days.title: HEADSTAND
days.blurb: a typeface, drawn in one day — a reverse-contrast circus slab, thick where letters should be thin, thin where they should be thick · every glyph built as geometry in Python (stems, slab serifs, rings, cuts) and compiled straight to a real font: 49 glyphs, one weight, ~6 KB, free under the OFL · the specimen page is a playbill you can retype · soundtrack is a mechanical rag whose B strain is the melody upside down · no font editor was opened

days.title: THE FOUNDRY
days.blurb: bells that have never existed, cast in mathematics and struck for the first time · a finite-element modal solver, validated against Lamb's exact 1882 sphere, casts the traditional minor-third church bell, then re-runs the 1985 Eindhoven hunt and designs a major-third bell on one desktop in an afternoon · eight bells scaled down a D major scale ring a plain course of Plain Bob Major, 112 changes, no row repeated · every sound computed from the metal's own physics, nothing recorded

days.title: ONE WATER
days.blurb: field recordings of a language family that has never existed · one invented ancestor (Proto-Wenic), two daughters derived by mechanical sound law — ordered, exceptionless, run over the whole lexicon, so every word was derived, not designed · the same ten-sentence tale told three times: north informant on 1955 field tape, south informant 1958, and the reconstructed ancestor, clean because it was never recorded · voices are phoneme-driven TTS auditioned by a universal phone recognizer; the tape wear is numpy · in the north, apocope built a case system nobody designed

days.title: THE LINGUIST
days.blurb: yesterday's language family, dug back up blind · a comparative-method solver written from scratch is handed only the two daughter wordlists — no ancestor, no laws — and must align cognates, extract correspondences, reconstruct the proto-lexicon and induce the ordered sound laws; then the sealed truth is opened and every segment graded · 506 segments: zero real errors — its only misses (a laryngeal's identity, *w behind v) were the two it had declared unknowable in advance, in writing · it postulated the lost laryngeal the way Saussure did in 1879 · both codices regenerate the daughters 115/115

days.title: WAKE
days.blurb: creatures evolved to swim, in water that pushes back · a D2Q9 lattice-Boltzmann ocean validated before any animal existed (viscosity to 0.055%, the Re=100 cylinder at drag 1.45 / Strouhal 0.163) · a creature here is only a shape that changes, and the change carries exactly zero momentum — it cannot push on itself, so every body length is taken from the water · 56 random genomes, 63 generations, fitness = distance swum and nothing else: the median rose 4.7x and straightness reached 1.00 without ever being rewarded · the champion is not a fish, it curls into a hydrofoil and rides its own vortex dipole · it lives on the page in a real fluid you can stir

days.title: GROWN
days.blurb: a typeface family grown, not drawn · every glyph is a bare public-domain skeleton dropped into a simulated nutrient bath: diffusion feeds the frontier, tips screen the hollows, and the growth throws thorns the way frost and coral do · photographed at four moments and traced into four real installable fonts — Accretion Seed, Sprout, Thicket, Overgrown — which nest cell for cell, because growth only ever adds · the specimen page grows your own words as you type them · the film's crackle is the accretion itself, cell counts driving grains · free under the OFL

days.title: TOLL
days.blurb: four bells cast from ice, rung until they broke · each bell is a finite-element model in real ice — and ice's sound speed is only 9% below bell bronze, so a fresh ice bell truly rings · re-solved at 22 stages of melting: the hum falls five semitones as the wall thins, the ring collapses from 3 seconds to a knock as the core warms (cited glacier acoustics), and every strike is checked against a tensile strength that weakens toward 0°C · the deaths are computed, not scripted — the treble shatters first, silences open in the change-ringing grid, the tenor tolls alone · path-traced in Blender, unlocked today · the page has a fifth bell you can ring yourself; it can only break if you ring it

links.label: the bell (ring it while it melts)

days.title: PHOTOTAXIS
days.blurb: a 20 cm pane of clear acrylic computed so that sunlight refracts into a luna moth on the wall · the exit face carries a 5.8 mm relief found by gradient descent through a differentiable ray tracer, then verified by an independent float64 simulation that shares no code with the designer — it caught a flipped refraction sign and a scheme of light-dumping cliffs before the surface was allowed to exist (final agreement 0.991) · the physics wrote the ending: a thin pane bends light nearly the same at every angle, so the moth never dissolves — it walks the wall at 2 mm a minute all afternoon, and for nine minutes stands exactly where it was drawn · the wall's light in the film is 24 million verified rays per frame, because even Blender's caustic solver could not converge this transport · the page runs the same optics live — drag the sun — and ships the STL: you can mill this window

days.title: MUSICA UNIVERSALIS
days.blurb: in 1619 Kepler claimed the planets play music; today a computer measured which intervals gravity actually keeps · 284,000 two-planet systems integrated on one GPU in 88 minutes, the period ratio swept across the musical scale like a piano, the eccentricity raised until only the protected survive · the survival map reads as music theory: towers of life at exactly 2:1 (the octave) and 3:2 (the fifth), a sea of death at the minor second, and an island at unison where planets survive by sharing one orbit, trading places like Janus and Epimetheus · verified against an independent float64 integrator, and in the chaotic frontier even the verifier disagrees with itself across tolerances, which is the honest finding: past the Lyapunov horizon only ensembles are facts · the film's score is generated from the survival data itself · the page is an instrument: place planets as notes, loudness is mass, gravity edits every melody, and every composition is a shareable URL

days.title: PLUVIAL
days.blurb: a typeface, left out in the rain for one hundred thousand years · the studio's own day-16 face (Headstand) cut again as stone mesas and eroded on the GPU — hydraulic droplets, scree slides, weathering, with a mass ledger closed to 8 parts per million · six moments of the decay traced back into real installable fonts: the family is PLUVIAL and the style names are the years of rain, 0 to 100,000, all six with identical spacing so the letters wear away without reflowing · and because rain destroys, the specimen carries what specimens never have: a mortality table, measured by two machine readers at every age · V dies first at year 2,800, mistaken for a Y; N dies into X; eight letters fall together at the 25,000-year cliff; at 100,000 years the last letter still reading its own name is A · the fonts are free (OFL), the readings and the whole table are on the page

links.label: the specimen (type on the ruins) + free fonts

days.title: THE SAME DRUM
days.blurb: Kac asked in 1966: can one hear the shape of a drum? Gordon, Webb and Wolpert answered no in 1992 — two different polygons whose membranes share every resonant frequency · today both are real playable drums: eigenmodes solved by finite elements (validated to 0.02% against 12-digit reference values, the pair isospectral to 2 parts per million across 25 modes), sound and ripples from the same eigenfunctions · plus a bestiary of drums nobody has ever heard — a chess knight, a star, a crescent, a club, a question mark whose fat dot rings barely higher than its narrow stem · nine drums in A-minor pentatonic, a composed peal, and a blind listening test that mathematics caps at a coin flip

links.label: the instrument (strike the drums + the test you cannot pass)

days.title: THE GRAVITY COMPUTER
days.blurb: a computer with no electricity in it: a five-bit binary counting machine inside a real rigid-body physics engine · one moving part per bit — a pivoted rocker latched by gravity alone (mass above the pivot, an inverted pendulum with two wells) · a falling marble flips the bit it lands on; a bit falling 1 to 0 hands the marble down the tower, and that handoff is the binary carry · 27 marbles in, 11011 out: 13 + 14 = 27 · the soundtrack is the collision log itself, one marimba note per flip, lower notes for higher bits, so the carry ripple at 15+1 plays a descending run the machine composed by arithmetic · exactly 50 flips required, exactly 50 performed, all 50 notes verified by FFT on the shipped master

days.title: THUNDER
days.blurb: you cannot hear the shape of a drum (day 26 proved it) — but you can hear the shape of lightning · every metre of a bolt fires its shock at the same instant, so the ear receives the channel sorted by distance: a sphere sweeping outward at 343 m/s, playing the bolt like a stylus plays a groove · today's bolt was grown by real dielectric breakdown on the GPU, roughened to the measured 16°-per-8-m tortuosity of actual lightning, and its thunder computed from nothing but that shape — 24,047 shock sources, atmospheric absorption, ground echo, two ears · machine-verified: onset = nearest point ÷ speed of sound, exactly; a dead-straight rod of equal length and energy makes ONE clap where the real bolt makes eight — the claps are the wiggles · the film's entire soundtrack is the computation; nothing was recorded

days.title: FILM
days.blurb: A movie with no pigment in it. A renderer that traces 81 wavelengths instead of RGB, pointed at the only things whose color is pure geometry: a prism, an oil slick, and a soap bubble that drains, turns Newton-black at 25 nanometers, and pops. The soundtrack is the light entering the camera, transposed down 40 octaves. Hold a bubble yourself — its colors come from the same physics table.

days.title: PELT
days.blurb: Why does the leopard have spots on its body and rings on its tail? One chemistry, two answers — and the animal never chose. A Turing system owns exactly one length; wrap it around a body and the pattern can only use waves that close up on themselves. Below a circumference of 0.8 wavelengths no such wave exists, so the only pattern left is one that runs across: a ring. Predicted 8.89, measured 9.20 on the tail. The mouse, smaller than one wavelength, grows nothing at all — and that silence is the loudest thing in the film. Reshape the animal yourself, regrow its coat, and watch the shape decide what it gets.

days.title: THE IMPOSSIBLE BELL
days.blurb: Every church bell plays a minor chord, and nobody chose that. A from-scratch finite-element solver plus an evolutionary shape search rediscovers the church bell from five numbers, solves the 500-year major-third problem, then casts a bell with harmonic-series partials 1:2:3:4:5 that sings like a string. The solver was validated against exact elasticity before any bell existed (cylinder torsion to 1e-6) · tuning errors measured on the finest mesh: 0.5, 0.4 and 2.5 cents, where a professional tuner works to about five · every note in the shipped piece verified against the score. Tap all three live; the film plays Ode to Joy on each foundry and lets you hear the third change.

days.title: ASCENT
days.blurb: A machine with no brain climbs the stairs. No sensors, no feedback, one motor at constant speed — just twelve link lengths, evolved across a million candidate designs, that gear a Jansen-class gait exactly to the building-code staircase: one crank revolution = four stairs. Verified in rigid-body physics, not animated: spring feet, real friction, a 14-step flight climbed at exact geared speed. The machine even fixes its own placement errors by pressing each stride into the riser — placed wrong on purpose, three machines converge to the same track. The staircase is the program. Watch the physics replay live and morph the leg from Jansen's beach numbers to the stair genome yourself.

days.title: SKYWRITING
days.blurb: A snowflake is a diary of its fall. On the night Sapporo took 60 cm of snow, a weather balloon radioed back the storm's temperature and humidity, layer by layer; that real sounding drives a mass-conserving snow-crystal model, and the crystal that lands 84 minutes later can be read outward like tree rings — a plate from the cold kilometers, arms from the −13 °C moist layer, edges sealed where the air went dry. Grown twice from the same seed it is identical to the last cell; split into two futures at 1,500 m, everything already frozen appears in both. Draw your own sky and grow the letter it would write.

days.title: WARBLE
days.blurb: Nobody has ever heard a snowflake: a 3 mm dendrite rings near 2.7 kHz, too small and too doomed to sound in air. But yesterday's crystals exist as exact geometry, so today they became instruments — each one's grown shape treated as a thin ice plate, its vibrational eigenmodes computed and struck like a bell. A perfect hexagon rings exactly degenerate mode pairs; the blizzard-grown crystals are slightly lopsided, so their pairs split and beat — the warble is the storm's own signature. Twelve bells, a found scale, and the middle movement rings plain hunt on four of them, with day 33's bit-identical twins as the same bell an octave apart.

days.title: A FIELD GUIDE TO THE FAUNA OF THE LENIA CONTINUUM
days.blurb: An expedition, not a design: 156,288 random worlds of Lenia (Chan's continuous cellular-automaton universe) were sown with living slop and left to fend for themselves. Whatever survived alone, held its shape and withstood rough handling was caught, measured and named — sixteen species with Latin binomials, engraved plates, field notes and a habitability chart, typeset as a 22-page Victorian monograph. The swiftest animal taken swims at 8.25 lattice-units per unit of time; one "still life" secretly creeps; two are corals. Every specimen is alive in the page's tank, running in your browser.

days.title: SÉANCE FOR AN EXTINCT ORCHESTRA
days.blurb: Five instruments that no longer exist — the glass armonica blamed for madness, the tromba marina the nuns bowed instead of forbidden trumpets, the serpent Berlioz insulted, the ophicleide born and dead in one lifetime, the baryton that existed for one prince — rebuilt as physical simulations: stick-slip friction, lip valves, a deliberately rattling bridge, ten sympathetic wires. Then the concert they never had: a passacaglia in D on a falling ground, until the candle goes out. Every one of the 285 notes machine-verified to sound in the master.

days.title: ECHOLOCATION
days.blurb: A cave you can only see with sound. You are a bat: every tap is a real acoustic wave, the 2D wave equation solved live on your GPU, and the rock exists only where the wavefront touches it, then fades. Water drips somewhere in warm light; find it. What you hear is not an effect: the same solver runs again, faster, from each click and records the pressure at your two ears, so the echo is the echo of this exact cave. Press B and play it blind.
